objective_for_doctor: A 72-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have lightheadedness/near-fainting, significant dyspnea, and palpitations.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi. I came in because I’ve been having significant trouble breathing, with lightheadedness like I might faint, and palpitations. It started after I used stimulant drugs and also recently took some decongestants or other substances that can make you feel “revved up.”

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—first, when did the symptoms start, and do they come in sudden episodes or are they constant? Also, have you had chest pain, sweating, or fainting completely?  
Doctor: If you can, please tell me your pulse/heart rate if you’ve checked it, and whether you have blacking out with position changes (standing up).  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: ECG (12-lead) and Orthostatic vitals.

They started recently—after the stimulant use and the decongestants/substances that can feel stimulating. It feels like it comes in episodes: my breathing gets really bad, I get palpitations, and I feel close to fainting, but I’m not sure it’s constant. I don’t have chest pain, but I do feel very sweaty sometimes; I have not fully fainted completely.  

I haven’t checked my pulse/heart rate. When I stand up, I do get more lightheaded like I might pass out, yes.

Doctor: Thanks—based on the episodic palpitations with sweating plus worsening on standing right after stimulants, I’m concerned about an arrhythmia or possibly stimulant-induced tachyarrhythmia, and also orthostatic hypotension. Do you have a history of heart disease/atrial fibrillation, and are you currently taking any beta-blockers/thyroid meds or anticoagulants?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel (electrolytes, glucose), CBC, Troponin, TSH, and Urine_toxicology (stimulants/decongestants).

I don’t have a known history of heart disease or atrial fibrillation. I’m not on any beta-blockers, thyroid medicine, or blood thinners/anticoagulants that I know of. I haven’t taken any medicines like that—mostly just the decongestants/substances that may be stimulating.

Doctor: I’m going to check a few more things—do you ever hear a racing/irregular heartbeat at rest, and do these episodes last minutes vs hours? Also, any fever, cough, or leg swelling/pain that could suggest infection or a clot?  
Doctor: If you’re able, I’d like your oxygen saturation and blood pressure/heart rate while lying down and standing; REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry and Repeat_Orthostatic_Vitals with continuous heart-rate monitoring.

Yes—when I’m resting I can feel my heart racing, and it feels kind of irregular sometimes. The episodes last minutes, not hours.  

No fever or cough. I don’t have leg swelling or leg pain. I don’t know my oxygen saturation or my exact blood pressure/heart rate measurements right now.

Doctor: Given stimulant/decongestant exposure, brief episodes of racing/irregular palpitations with diaphoresis, and orthostatic worsening, I’m most concerned for a paroxysmal supraventricular tachyarrhythmia (e.g., SVT) or atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, with possible dehydration/orthostatic hypotension. I need the ECG/orthostatics and labs urgently; can you confirm if you are currently having symptoms right now (yes/no) so we triage immediately?
Yes, I’m having symptoms right now—my breathing feels very difficult, and I feel the palpitations with near-fainting/lightheadedness.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—right now I need you to stay seated and I’m going to treat this as potentially dangerous until we prove otherwise; do you have severe chest pressure, blue lips, or actual fainting/near-blackout where you can’t stay upright?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any known heart rhythm history or blood thinner use, and what exact stimulant/decongestant (name/dose) did you take and when?

No severe chest pressure. I don’t have blue lips that I’ve noticed. I haven’t fully fainted or blacked out—I’m able to stay upright, but I feel like I’m close.

I don’t have known rhythm history and I’m not on blood thinners. I used stimulant drugs recently and I also took decongestants/substances that can be stimulating, but I don’t remember the exact names and doses off the top of my head.

Doctor: I’m going to assume this is unstable until proven otherwise—do you have an Apple Watch/phone pulse read, and can you tell me your current age and any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or prior fainting?  
Doctor: While you answer, I need immediate results: do you consent to go for ECG interpretation now and we’ll repeat vitals continuously?

I’m 72. I don’t have an Apple Watch or a phone pulse read. I don’t know of any history of high blood pressure or diabetes, and I don’t have prior fainting history—just these episodes recently.  

Yes, I consent to have the ECG interpreted now and repeat my vitals continuously.

Doctor: I need two quick details: are you on any inhalers or antidepressants (especially stimulants, ADHD meds, or cocaine/amphetamines), and do you have any allergy or kidney disease?  
Doctor: Meanwhile, REQUEST TEST: Continuous_Telemetry/monitoring during orthostatic vitals and REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to assess dyspnea causes while we wait for the ECG.  
Doctor: Based on stimulant/decongestant-triggered, brief episodes of racing/irregular palpitations with diaphoresis and near-syncope on standing, and presuming this could be SVT/AF with RVR, I’m ready to treat as paroxysmal tachyarrhythmia until the ECG says otherwise.  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachyarrhythmia (SVT) or atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response—stimulant/decongestant-induced, with orthostatic intolerance/possible dehydration.

[DDX]
1. Atrial fibrillation
